interpretation.diagram_classification: Biblical-geographical / typological diagram, probably a plan of the Israelite camp in the wilderness, with the tribes arranged around the Tabernacle and the priesthood
interpretation.interpretation: The diagram is a concentric scheme. The central circle carries the words "Habitacio", "Legis" and "Sacerdotuas", which I read as the dwelling of the law and of the priesthood, that is, the Tabernacle or sanctuary at the centre. The middle ring carries further words in red, including "Habitacio", "Propheta" and what may be "Moabit" or "Amon" (the readings are uncertain). The outer ring is divided by radial lines into rectangular compartments. These are placed at the top, upper left, upper right, lower right and bottom, and they contain text that appears to begin with "Porta" or "Pera" ("gate"). The most probable reading is a plan of the encampment of Israel or of the Holy City, with gates arranged around a central sanctuary. The inscriptions are probably the names of the gates or tribes, with a possible orientation to the four cardinal directions. The reading "aquilonii" (north) in the top compartment supports a cardinal orientation. A ring of gates around a sacred centre is also a familiar pattern in diagrams of the heavenly Jerusalem and of Ezekiel's temple vision. I cannot say with confidence which of these the scheme follows.
interpretation.evidence: Visible: concentric circles; a central circle with a dotted inner contour; an outer ring divided into compartments by black radial lines; red text along the middle ring. Written: "Habitacio", "Legis 7", "Sacerdotuas", "Propheta", "Porta", "aquilonii". Most of the text is faded or illegible and my Step 1 readings are tentative. For example, "Pera aquilonii", "Moabit", "Amon" and "Raphaim" are uncertain, and Step 1 gives the compartments inconsistent names. Step 1 also does not clearly separate the red and black texts or the 7-like sign (possibly an abbreviation for "et"). The identification with a camp plan or a Jerusalem-type scheme comes from external knowledge of medieval diagrams and is not confirmed by a legible title. The names "Moabit", "Amon" and "Raphaim" would point to the peoples of the Promised Land, which fits a biblical-geographical context, but this depends on uncertain readings. No source is named because I am not confident of one.
